answer: One identity locks 70 credits for one wharf muster slot. Entry needs a key-bound wander pass: its serial, key, and epoch enter a nectar ledger, and each attendee at the wharf draws one nectar ration. An auditor rechecks the roll; a serial under a second key, or a ration without attendance, burns the bond. The first fee is 32; the kth fake pays 32+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7025 and 1000 fakes pay 3,528,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-stand-in ring fails: one stand-in holds a pass per window, so it needs 1000 hires. An honest identity pays 32 once, locks 70 once, and recovers it after audit.
